title: Geo heartbeat queueing caused region mis-selection and fallback variant cascade
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2025-02-18 a control-plane backlog caused geo heartbeat acknowledgements to be delayed and queued. Stale drain/decommission signals combined with delayed heartbeats led the smart router to prefer wrong regions for a subset of tenants, triggering a cascade of fallback model variants and elevated error and cost rates. This ticket captures the incident, immediate mitigations, root-cause analysis, and follow-up engineering work.
timeline: 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC: Alert - 5xx spike and elevated latency observed for hosted-api in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (paginated alert from routing-error-rate dashboard).
2025-02-18 09:18 UTC: Oncall investigation - discovered increased fallback rates to smaller model variants and cross-region request shifts for many customers.
2025-02-18 09:27 UTC: Control plane queue metric (cp.update_queue_length) spiked due to surge in node lifecycle events from automated maintenance. Heartbeat ACKs were queued and delayed.
2025-02-18 09:35 UTC: Rolled back recent aggressive decommission flags pushed by maintenance job; began draining false-positive tombstones.
2025-02-18 10:02 UTC: Mitigation - enforced conservative routing policy: disable variant-escape fallbacks for affected customers and add temporary routing TTL extension.
2025-02-18 11:00 UTC: Error rates returned near baseline after mitigations; continued monitoring for 48 hours.
2025-02-20 15:00 UTC: Deep-dive identified control-plane write amplification as root contributor to heartbeat queueing. Prepared long-term remediation plan.
root_cause: A maintenance job created a burst of node lifecycle updates that overloaded the control-plane update queue. The router relies on timely heartbeat ACKs and tombstone consistency; queued ACKs caused outdated tombstones to persist in the cluster view. The compatibility-mapping logic treats stale tombstones as decommission signals for specific region/tier mappings, resulting in requests being rerouted away from healthy capacity. The combination of reroutes and the existing fallback policy (automatic swap to lighter model variants when a region is perceived unhealthy) created a positive feedback loop that amplified traffic to lower-capacity variants, increasing latency and 5xxs.
immediate_actions: Rolled back the maintenance job and cleared control-plane update backlog (2025-02-18).
Applied a temporary conservative routing policy: extended routing TTL to tolerate delayed heartbeats by 30s and disabled aggressive variant fallback for affected tenant segments (2025-02-18).
Notified affected customers and offered credits where SLA thresholds were breached (2025-02-18 through 2025-02-21).
Added a short-circuit in router to ignore tombstones older than 2 minutes unless confirmed by a second independent signal (hotfix deployed 2025-02-19).
long_term_fixes: Add backpressure and rate-limit to node lifecycle/maintenance jobs to avoid write storms to control plane (planned for runtime-1.20.patch1).
Make tombstone and heartbeat processing idempotent and vector-clocked so delayed ACKs do not flip region affinity unexpectedly (design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4498).
Introduce a routing circuit-breaker that detects rapid-redistribution of traffic and temporarily pins region selection while control-plane stability is confirmed.
Improve observability: new dashboard tiles for cp.update_queue_length, tombstone-age distribution, and variant-fallback rate per region (dashboards added).
Add canary for variant-fallback policy changes and a throttle window that prevents more than 10% of a tenant's traffic from switching variants within 60s.

notes: Decision: prefer slower, more conservative routing behavior rather than fast variant swaps when control-plane signals are unstable.
Trade-off: extending routing TTL increases time to detect true failures but avoids large-scale fallback churn; chosen as default guardrail for high-traffic tenants.
Reviewed with product and ops; agreed to ship circuit-breaker and write-rate limit before summer traffic ramp.
